_comment: Example config for mdns_dns_sync. One file per agent instance (per VLAN). Strip _comment fields before deploying.
_comment_interface: IPv4 or IPv6 address of the local interface this agent will listen on. zeroconf scopes its multicast group membership to this interface only.
_comment_server: DNS server (BIND) that accepts dynamic updates with the TSIG key below.
_comment_keyfile: BIND-format TSIG keyfile, passed to nsupdate -k. Same format as ipv6_dns_sync's .mykey: key "name" { algorithm hmac-sha256; secret "..."; };
_comment_domain: Forward zone to update. mDNS names ending in .local are rewritten by replacing .local with this domain.
_comment_publish_v4: If true, also publish A records and (when reverse_zones_v4 covers them) v4 PTRs. Default false matches the v6-only behaviour of ipv6_dns_sync.
_comment_reverse_zones: IPv6 CIDRs the agent is authoritative for. v6 PTRs are only written for addresses inside one of these. The reverse zone name is derived from each CIDR (must be nibble-aligned, which BIND delegations always are).
_comment_reverse_zones_v4: IPv4 CIDRs the agent is authoritative for. v4 PTRs (in-addr.arpa) are only written for addresses inside one of these. Only relevant when publish_v4 is true.
_comment_filters: Optional. The agent receives mDNS announcements from EVERY interface in the container's network namespace (a known zeroconf/Linux multicast quirk - binding to an interface IP only controls send, not receive). Use these filters to scope each per-VLAN agent to addresses that actually belong on its VLAN. String-prefix match.
_comment_filters_v4: IPv4 counterparts. Only relevant when publish_v4 is true. Same defense-in-depth role as include_prefixes for v6.
_comment_allowed_hosts: Optional allowlist of short hostnames (without .local). When present, announcements from other hosts on the link are ignored. When absent/null, all announcements on the link are accepted. Use null on trusted management VLANs; use a list on VLANs that may carry guest/IoT devices.
_comment_prefer_named_ptrs: When true (default), hosts whose short name looks like a canonical UUID (8-4-4-4-12 hex, e.g. dd533fcf-723d-4621-bb57-33dccb62786e) won't claim PTR records that another host already published. Friendly hostnames always win for PTRs; forward records (AAAA/A) are still published under both names so resolution works either way. Common with HomePods and other Apple devices that announce themselves under both their friendly name and an internal UUID.
_comment_host_timeout: Seconds. If a host hasn't announced anything for this long, its records (v4 and v6) are removed. Catches sleeping laptops that don't send mDNS goodbye packets.
